result.summary: Severe vertical structural cracking running through the central architectural features and brickwork of the facade, originating near the gable peak and extending downward past the window opening.

findings.location: Center of the brick facade, passing through the upper gable apex, decorative stone niche, pediment, and extending down below the arched window
probable_causes: Structural overloading or roof spreading forces
recommended_actions: Engage a structural engineer specializing in historic preservation immediately
Install tell-tale crack monitors to track active movement
Perform non-destructive testing to assess wall tie and internal stability
Implement temporary shoring if ongoing movement is detected

result.monitoring_plan: Install mechanical or electronic crack width gauges across the vertical fracture at multiple elevations. Record measurements and take dated photographs bi-weekly to determine if the crack is actively widening or stabilizing.
result.limitations: Visual assessment is based solely on exterior photographic evidence without direct physical access, material testing, or sub-surface investigation.
